meta.title: Bonnie's Long Journey
meta.author: LiamBox
meta.description: Departure day. Bonnie, 23, has one stubborn rule for travel: flawless manners, total composure, and nobody inconvenienced. Twenty-two hours, seven chapters, and a great many drinks she is too polite to refuse. Placeholder wording.

characters.name: Bonnie
characters.notes: Twenty-three, leaving for a university exchange semester. Lives with her parents. A committed people-pleaser with a stubborn streak.

characters.name: Irina
characters.notes: The Higgins' daughter, a student Bonnie's age. Loud, warm, awake.

leakOnFail.bladder: That was a spasm. A little got out. I am SO sorry.

overflow.bladder: There is no more room. NONE. Some of that just left.

triggers.bladder: Hello again. Remember me? I have news.
This is no longer a request.

minigame.prompt: Too many twinges at once! Tap them away!

triggers.bladder: Just let go. Right here. Who would ever know?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The red digits on the nightstand click over to 4:10. Under the blanket, Bonnie curls her toes and bites her lip.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She has not been since yesterday afternoon. That was the challenge she set herself: flawless manners, total composure, and nobody inconvenienced. It is going badly.
lines.bladder: I filed a complaint at midnight. Nobody answered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Through the wall, Dad's snoring is slow and even. Chloe's room next door is quiet. The taxi comes at eight. If she is ever going to go, it is now. Silently.
lines.bladder: There is a bathroom downstairs. Fourteen steps. I counted.

choices.text: Slide out of bed slowly. Every spring of this mattress is a tattletale.
Just get UP. Speed over silence. Not one more minute.
Lie still one more minute and listen to the house. Be sure.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The landing is cold under her feet. Chloe's door is open a hand's width.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She already knows which board outside Chloe's door complains. She steps over it.

lines.speaker: chloe
lines.text: Mmh... Bonnie...?
lines.bladder: She's awake. We are DONE. Abort, or run for it?

choices.text: Slip back to my room and KEEP HOLDING. The record is not over.

texts.freeze: Freeze. Wait. Let her settle back into sleep, then carry on.
texts.push_on: Whisper "just getting water" and keep walking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bonnie eases the door shut and climbs back into bed like someone defusing it. Hard mode. Nobody asked her to. That is rather the point.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wave arrives on schedule.
lines.bladder: You had ONE chance. You were RIGHT THERE.

choices.text: Face it. Ride out the wave.
This is absurd. Go. Now. Properly this time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wave passes. The record stands, and so does the problem. Bonnie stares at the ceiling until the alarm goes. Everything from here will be harder. She is, somehow, pleased.
lines.bladder: I want it noted that I objected.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The record can stand some other night. Bonnie is out of bed and past Chloe's door before she can talk herself out of it.
lines.bladder: Finally. FINALLY. Left at the banister.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Fourteen stairs. The fourth and the seventh creak; she mapped them years ago, coming home late.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every step down is a small negotiation.
lines.bladder: Faster. No. Slower. No. FASTER.

choices.text: One stair at a time, weight on the banister, slow as syrup.
Skip the fourth and the seventh. Muscle memory.

minigame.prompt: Slowly. One stair at a time. Slowly!

choices.text: Sit down and go step by step on my hands. Undignified. Silent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere above, bedsprings shift. A floorboard answers the one she just stepped on.
lines.bladder: They heard that. Everyone heard that.

texts.freeze: FREEZE. Become furniture. Wait for the silence to heal.
texts.push_on: Push on. So close. Fortune favors the desperate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The door closes with a click she feels in her teeth. The lock turns. Nobody is coming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The pipes in this house carry sound like a telephone.
lines.bladder: I do not care about the pipes. I have never cared less about anything.

choices.text: Now. Speed over silence. Not one more breath.
Ease down and go quietly, stopping dead whenever the house stirs.

minigame.prompt: Quietly! And STOP if anyone calls!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Relief. Complete, ridiculous, hard-earned relief. Bonnie leans on the sink and grins at nobody.
lines.bladder: Thank you. I take back most of what I said.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One problem left: the cistern in this house fills like a jet engine.

choices.text: Don't flush. Lid down, leave silently, flush 'casually' once everyone is up.
Flush and sprint. Beat the pipes back up the stairs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Back under the blanket, nobody the wiser. The clock is reset. The real journey starts at eight, and it is twenty hours long.
lines.bladder: Enjoy it. You will not hear from me for at least an hour.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By eight the house is loud with a family seeing someone off. Chloe, full of espresso, is fastening the back of Bonnie's travel jumpsuit: one long row of tiny, stubborn buttons.

lines.speaker: chloe
lines.text: Hold STILL! You'll look amazing. Like a superhero.
lines.bladder: Superheroes can't get out of these either, you know.

choices.text: "Chloe, gently! Go easy."
Endure it. Smile. Say nothing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Downstairs Mom has laid out everything the kitchen owns.

lines.speaker: mom
lines.text: Drink up, sweetheart, you have such a long flight. Hydration is everything!
lines.bladder: She means well. She always means well. That is the problem.

choices.text: The small juice. Modest, quick, defensible.
The green tea. Mom's pride. Warm, generous, and it runs straight through.
The big smoothie. Heavy, slow, an anchor in the stomach.
All of it. Every glass. Make Mom glow on departure day.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.text: Wheels up in ten! Everyone use the bathroom, it's a long drive.
lines.bladder: He said EVERYONE. That includes us. That is practically an order.

texts.hover: Hover on the edge of yes... then wave them on. Almost. ALMOST.
texts.busy: Make myself useful instead: carry the bags, check the passport, busy hands.

lines.speaker: dad
lines.text: Right: interstate or the bypass? One's longer, one's bumpier, and I can never remember which is worse at this hour.
lines.bladder: Whichever has fewer bumps. Please. I am begging you.

choices.text: "The interstate, Dad."
"Take the bypass."
"You choose!"

lines.speaker: mom
lines.text: That coffee went right through me! Bonnie, come on, last chance before the queue!
lines.bladder: LAST CHANCE. She said last chance. Did you hear the words?

texts.refuse: "I'm fine, go ahead!" and a little wave.
texts.hover: Take one step after her... and stop to check the departure board instead.
texts.busy: Offer to watch everyone's bags. Somebody has to.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The queue snakes through six lanes of tape. Forty minutes, the sign says. The sign is an optimist.
lines.bladder: Forty minutes. Standing. On tile.

choices.text: Stand perfectly still, like a mannequin of a polite young woman.
The subtle shuffle-clamp. Shuffle, clamp. Shuffle, clamp.
Lean a hip against the luggage cart. It looks casual. It is load-bearing.

lines.speaker: tsa
lines.text: Step through. Arms up.
lines.bladder: Arms UP? Does he know what he is asking?

choices.text: Smile at the officer. Comply crisply. Be forgettable.
Move a touch too fast through the scanner. Get it OVER with.
Ask for the seated pat-down instead. Sitting is... strategic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In her bag: one oversized iced tea, bought ten minutes ago, eight dollars, untouched.

lines.speaker: tsa
lines.text: No liquids past this point, miss. Drink it or bin it. Your call.
lines.bladder: Bin it. BIN IT. It was only eight dollars.

choices.text: Chug it. All of it. Right here at the barrier, like a legend.
Tip it into the bin, and feel the waste of it stain the halo.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Seat 34A. A window, a tray table, and between Bonnie and the aisle a large businessman who is asleep before the doors close.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Long flight, eh.
lines.bladder: Fourteen hours. Behind a wall. A wall that snores.

choices.text: Perfect. A wall of businessman means nobody can see me squirm.
Do the math again. Properly this time. Know exactly where I stand.
Sleep NOW while it's quiet. Sleep is time travel for the desperate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The numbers were not comforting.

lines.speaker: attendant
lines.text: And to drink? We have tea, coffee, juice... or I can do the large water.
lines.bladder: Say "nothing, thank you." It is three words. You know all three.

triggers.bladder: Your hand is ALREADY reaching for it. Stop being so nice!

choices.text: "Tea, please." Warm, modest... and a deceptively large pot.
"Coffee." Small cup. Sharp price: it goes straight through.
"Juice, thank you." Sweet, heavy, and somehow 400 ml.
"Just the water." The LARGE water. The only size they carry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hour five. The seatbelt sign chimes and the cabin drops a foot. The belt sits exactly where she wishes it did not.
lines.bladder: WHO APPROVED THIS? Who is flying this thing?

choices.text: Grip both armrests and ride it like a rodeo of pure regret.

minigame.prompt: Brace! Keep me level through the bumps!

choices.text: Press the blanket down over my lap. Pressure against pressure.
Hum the safety video jingle. Panic, but organized.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The businessman wakes, stretches, and shuffles off toward the lavatory. For the first time in eight hours, the aisle is open.
lines.bladder: The wall is GONE. Go. GO. This is not a drill.

texts.refuse: Stay put. "I'm fine!" she tells nobody at all.
texts.hover: Unbuckle... half stand... and sit back down as he returns.
texts.busy: Tidy the seat pocket instead. Fold the blanket. Very busy.

choices.text: Go. A hurried half-visit, before the queue at the lavatory door loses patience.

lines: Miss? Is everything all right in there?
Excuse me, there is a queue out here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Forty minutes of descent. The pilot points out landmarks. The plane leans, slowly, onto every one of them.
lines.bladder: Every. Single. Landmark.

choices.text: Nod at every landmark. Smile. Be a lovely window companion.
Fake sleep. Rude-adjacent, but faces can't leak secrets while unconscious.
Count the seconds between waves. Knowledge is power?

minigame.prompt: Count, then. In order. Ignore me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Landed. A new clock on the wall says 8:30 in the evening. Her body has stopped believing in clocks.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.text: Purpose of visit?
lines.bladder: Tell him the truth. "To find a bathroom."

choices.text: "Exchange program!" Bright. Crisp. Rehearsed in the mirror weeks ago.
Answer in the fewest possible syllables. Words shake things loose.
Compliment his stamp technique. Charm is a pressure valve.

scenes.title: 8:45 PM — The Sign and the Text

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Past the desk, a restroom sign glows like a lighthouse. Her phone buzzes: "We're outside, love!! 🎉"
lines.bladder: Lighthouse. LIGHTHOUSE. Steer toward the lighthouse.

texts.refuse: Type "Coming!!" and walk straight past the sign.
texts.hover: Drift toward the sign... and let the crowd carry her on.
texts.busy: Find a trolley first. Then the right carousel. Then it is too late.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her suitcase comes round the carousel: fifty pounds, packed by someone who feared for her survival abroad.
lines.bladder: Do NOT lift that. Lifting is pushing. Pushing is my department.

choices.text: One clean deadlift, exhale like a powerlifter, DONE.
Let it go around again and catch it at a better angle next lap.
Ask the kind man beside me for help, with my best exhausted smile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Arrivals. A sprinting figure and a slower, wider one behind her.

lines.speaker: irina
lines.text: BONNIE! BONNIE!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mrs. Higgins arrives second and hugs first: a fierce, two-armed squeeze, right around the middle.
lines.bladder: ABORT HUG. ABORT HUG.

lines.speaker: bonnie
lines.text: Hnnng... HI!

choices.text: Hug back. Breathe out. Smile. Be delighted.
Get a hand out first and turn it into a handshake. Then a wave.

lines.speaker: irina
lines.text: How do you even go to the bathroom in that suit?

lines.speaker: bonnie
lines.text: I didn't.
lines.bladder: At LAST. Someone is asking the right questions.

lines.speaker: mrs_higgins
lines.text: Want to go before we drive, love? It's forty minutes.

texts.refuse: "I'm perfectly fine!" Voice up half an octave.
texts.hover: "Oh, maybe I... no. No, let's go, you've waited long enough."
texts.busy: Insist on wheeling the suitcase to the car herself.

lines.speaker: mrs_higgins
lines.text: Coastal road or the tunnel, love? One's ever so pretty, the other's quick... though with the roadworks lately, honestly, who knows.
lines.bladder: Quick. QUICK. Nobody has ever needed pretty less.

choices.text: "The coastal road sounds lovely."
"The tunnel, maybe? Quickest is best."
"Surprise me!"

lines.speaker: mrs_higgins
lines.text: Sit, sit! You must be PARCHED after that flight.

lines.speaker: irina
lines.text: I'm bursting!
lines.bladder: SHE gets to say it. Out loud. Just like that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Irina thunders upstairs. A pot of tea the size of a lighthouse lands on the table.

lines.speaker: mrs_higgins
lines.text: Milk? Sugar? Drink up, love.

choices.text: Down it: graceful, grateful, gone. Nobody with a problem drinks like that.
Sip it slowly: polite, and stalling for dear life.
Nurse this one forever. Tiny sips, long stories, buy every possible second.
"I'm so sorry, the journey has absolutely wrecked me. Could I possibly just... go up to bed?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The guest room is lovely. The catch arrives with the towels: the only working bathroom upstairs is the en-suite off Irina's room.

lines.speaker: irina
lines.text: Just come through whenever! I sleep like the dead.
lines.bladder: Through HER ROOM. Past her BED. In the DARK.

choices.text: "No problem at all!" A sentence so false it should be arrested.
Stay up a while getting to know her. Friendship is politeness too.
Scout the hallway quietly first. Know the terrain. Count the creaks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Irina does not sleep like the dead. Irina plays music and talks through the wall, cheerfully, at length.
lines.bladder: She is AWAKE. The door is right there and she is AWAKE.

choices.text: Wait her out. The record grows with every minute.
Pace the room in tiny circles. Movement is management.
Lie perfectly still and go somewhere else in my head. A beach. A DRY beach.

minigame.prompt: Dry beach. Count the palm trees. In order.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two in the morning. The music has stopped. Twenty-two hours. She is a marvel of human engineering, and the dam is creaking.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three ways through this. None of them dignified.
lines.bladder: Pick one. ANY one. I vote for all three at once.

choices.text: Go. Now. Through her room, silent as a guilty thought.
Hold until her morning run. Four more hours. The PERFECT record.
The window. The garden. The dark. ...I am not a garden person. Am I?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Irina's door opens without a sound. The room is all shapes: a bed, a chair, a strip of light under the far door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She counted the creaks earlier. That helps. A little.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere in the dark, breathing. Slow. Probably asleep.
lines.bladder: Probably. PROBABLY is good enough. Walk.

choices.text: Step. Pause. Step. Read the breathing like sonar.
...no. Back out. The dawn plan.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Halfway. The strip of light is three steps away. The bed creaks behind her.
lines.bladder: THREE STEPS. I can see the door. I can SEE it.

choices.text: The last three steps. Slow as continental drift.
Just GO. Two quick steps and in.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bonnie sits on the edge of the bed, breathes slowly, and waits. The waves come on the hour, each one taller.
lines.bladder: This is not a plan. This is a hostage situation.

choices.text: Face it. Fight the wave through this whole hour.

minigame.prompt: The wave! I am springing leaks! Patch them!

choices.text: This is insane. Go NOW, through her room, before I shatter.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At exactly 6:58 the front door downstairs clicks shut. Footsteps crunch on gravel and fade.
lines.bladder: The house is EMPTY. The house is empty!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 6:58, and no footsteps on the gravel. Irina has skipped her run. She is downstairs cracking eggs for her new friend.
lines.bladder: She stayed in. For YOU. This is what being nice gets us.

choices.text: Walk to it. Slowly. Regally. This porcelain has been earned.
Through her room NOW, while she's downstairs. Last chance.
Go down to breakfast. Endure. Wait for the house to empty.
Ask. Just... ask. Out loud. Like a person.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sash lifts without a sound. Below: a trellis, a hedge, a great deal of dark.
lines.bladder: I have no objections. None. I have NEVER been less picky.

choices.text: Down the trellis. Behind the hedge. May the rosebush forgive me.
...I am not a garden person. The bedroom route. Final answer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It stops being a decision. Bonnie goes rigid mid-breath, every muscle she owns clamped around one last, failing idea.
lines.bladder: I can't. I'm sorry. I held as long as I could. I really, really did.

lines.speaker: bonnie
lines.text: No. No, no, no. Not now. Please. Thirty more seconds. I will do anything.
lines.bladder: You said that at four this morning. I have nothing left to give you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her eyes sting. All those hours of flawless manners, and the one thing she cannot be polite to is her own body.
lines.bladder: It is not your fault. It is not mine either. We were both very brave and very stubborn.

lines.speaker: bonnie
lines.text: ...Okay. Okay. I know. I'm sorry too.
lines.bladder: Letting go now. Don't look at anybody.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A sideways look. "You keep shifting about. Everything alright?"
lines.bladder: Tell them. They ASKED. It would be rude not to answer honestly.

texts.admit: Admit to 'a little travel fatigue.' Vague. Deniable.
texts.double_down: "Me? I'm WONDERFUL. Actually, is there a drink? I'd LOVE one."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: "You've gone pale, and you're trembling. What is going on?"
lines.bladder: This is it. Say the word. It is one word.

texts.admit: Admit it, barely a whisper: "...I could use a stop. Soon. Please."
texts.double_down: "Just the air conditioning!" and a laugh that fools nobody.

endings.title: The Perfect Record
endings.text: She walks down the hallway on shaking legs, locks the door, leans on the vanity, and finally lets go. It is the most colossal, silent and hard-earned relief of her life. She washes her hands, looks at her tired, victorious reflection, and smiles. The perfect record stands.

endings.title: Silent as a Guilty Thought
endings.text: The en-suite door closes behind her without a click. Irina never stirs. Twenty-two hours end in the dark, in someone else's bathroom, in absolute silence. Nobody will ever know. She almost wishes somebody could.

endings.title: Like a Person
endings.text: "Could I use your bathroom?" Six words. Nobody gasps. Somebody says "of course, love, second door." It turns out that was allowed the entire time. The record is over, and Bonnie cannot remember why it mattered.

endings.title: A Garden Person After All
endings.text: Behind the hedge, under the stars, in a country she has known for six hours. The rosebush keeps her secret. The halo does not survive the trellis, but the record, technically, does.

endings.title: "Oh! It's You"
endings.text: The lamp clicks on. Irina blinks at her from the pillow, entirely unbothered. "Bathroom's through there. I TOLD you to just come through." Bonnie makes it, with a witness and without her dignity. Irina is asleep again before the door closes.

endings.title: "Just Go, Love"
endings.text: Somebody finally says it out loud, kindly and firmly, and steers her toward the nearest door. It is mortifying for about four seconds and then it is the best thing that has ever happened to her. The record ends early, by popular demand.

endings.title: Not Quite
endings.text: Control gives out before the journey does. Nothing a change of clothes and a very long shower cannot fix, but the perfect record is over. She will tell this story at parties in about ten years.

scorecard.label: Sneaked a visit on the plane
